title: On ${\rm b}^{\ast}$-Coloring and $z$-Coloring of graphs with high girth
summary: In a proper vertex coloring $c$ of a graph $G$, a vertex $u$ is called a b-vertex if $u$ is adjacent to a vertex in every other color class. A ${\rm b}^{\ast}$-coloring is a proper coloring in which a b-vertex is adjacent to a b-vertex in every other color class. A Grundy coloring is a proper coloring obtained by the First-Fit (greedy) coloring procedure. A $z$-coloring of $G$ is a ${\rm b}^{\ast}$-coloring that is also a Grundy coloring.
